pr_body:
This PR adds the ability to use non-local templates when opening a PR. It is mostly a copy of the work done for issue create templates.

Closes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/838

issue_context.title: Pull request template is not used when creating a pull request in an organization with health files
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

Configured editor is not populated with contents of pull request template when running

```
$ gh pr create
```

to create a pull request in a repository that does not have  a pull request template defined in `.github`, but has a pull request template defined in a `.github` repository within the same organization (as laid out [here](https://help.github.com/en/github/building-a-strong-community/creating-a-default-community-health-file).



Running

```
$ gh --version
```

yields

```
gh version 0.7.0 (2020-04-22)
https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v0.7.0
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Run

    ```
    $ git clone git@github.com:ergebnis/composer-normalize.git
    ```

    to clone [`ergebnis/composer-normalize`](https://github.com/ergebnis/composer-normalize), a repository that does not define its own pull request template, but has a pull request template defined in [`ergebnis/.github`](https://github.com/ergebnis/.github).

2. Run

     ```
     $ git checkout -b fix/foo
     $ touch foo
     $ git add foo
     $ git commit -m "Foo"
     ```

    to create a new branch, create a new file, and commit it.

3. Run

    ```
    $ gh pr create
    ```

    to create a new pull request.

4. Press `enter` to use suggested title
5. Press `e` to launch configured editor

### Expected behavior

Editor is populated with content of pull request template defined in `.github` repository for corresponding organization

### Actual behaviour

Editor is **not** populated with content of pull request template defined in `.github` repository for corresponding organization.
comments:
(According to me, this is not exactly a bug, but a feature request)  
The program currently uses the local files of the repo to find the issue and PR templates.  
For this(getting issue and PR templates from the org) will require us to pull the required files from the remote org, and then use them.

@AliabbasMerchant From just recently there is an API specifically for getting issue templates. The said API is an internal preview phase, so only we can access it. We might explore moving to this API in a future release, although I can't tell you about the time frame for that. We will keep this thread updated!

I just stumbled upon this issue as well. As this seems not to be solved, what are the plans for this "feature/bug"? Or is this already available and I'm blind to see/find it?

For me even another/alternative way to have some sort of "global templates" would to be have an equivalent to ~/.gitmessage, e.g. checking for ~/.github, which in turn could be a clone of an arbitrary community health files repo (or even a particular branch therein).

@mrolli Sorry; we are still working on providing a GitHub API for this. The API for Issue templates has already shipped and `gh issue create` uses it since v1.6, but that does not include pull requests, so we're limited to looking up PR templates on disk as before.

@mislav 

Awesome! Any update on when this will be available in the main branch of releases of the cli?

review_comments: I moved this work into the `list` functions so that they would both have the same function signatures.
